        Idea:
Build `megaplan cloud` — a new subpackage at `megaplan/cloud/` that provides a built-in, provider-agnostic cloud runner wired into the existing megaplan CLI. This is sprint 1 of a two-sprint effort; the goal here is operational parity with the existing Railway setup at `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`, nothing more.

### What exists today (to be generalised)
The folder `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` contains a working but hardcoded Railway deployment. Read every file there during prep. Key pieces:
- `Dockerfile` — Ubuntu 22.04 + pyenv/Python 3.11 + nvm/Node 20 + codex CLI + claude CLI + megaplan from git
- `entrypoint.sh` — idempotent boot: codex auth (OPENAI_API_KEY), codex `config.toml` (model=gpt-5.4, reasoning=high, sandbox_mode=danger-full-access, approval_policy=never), megaplan install/upgrade from `MEGAPLAN_REF`, megaplan config (all phases→codex, auto_approve=true, robustness=standard), repo clone, installs `mp-run`/`mp-supervise`/`mp-heartbeat` wrapper scripts (currently embedded as heredocs), starts tmux sessions `agent` and `heartbeat`, starts healthserver
- `healthserver.py` — tiny HTTP server on :8080 for Railway healthcheck
- `railway.toml` — build/deploy config, healthcheck, restart policy
- `chain.sh` — thin shim around `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain.yaml`
- `chain.yaml.example` — chain spec format
- `README.md` — recipes for status/attach/resume/abort/restart/teardown that need to become subcommands

Hardcoded things to parameterise: `banodoco/reigh-app.git`, `/workspace/reigh-app`, `gpt-5.4` model, `high` reasoning, `[REDACTED]` email, all-phases→codex routing, `standard` robustness. Bug to fix: Claude Code CLI is installed in the image but the entrypoint never authenticates it — add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` auth path.

### Sprint 1 deliverables
1. New subpackage `megaplan/cloud/` parallel to `megaplan/loop/` and `megaplan/chain.py`, with:
   - Package resources: ported Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, healthserver.py. Extract the mp-run/mp-supervise/mp-heartbeat bash scripts (currently embedded as heredocs in entrypoint.sh) into their own files under `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/`.
   - Spec loader for `cloud.yaml` (schema covers at minimum: `provider`, `repo.url`/`branch`, `agents.default` + optional per-phase map, `codex.model` + `reasoning`, `mode` = auto|chain|idle, `auto.idea_file`, `auto.robustness`, `chain.spec`, `megaplan.ref`, `resources.volume`/`port`, `secrets` name list). PyYAML is not yet a dependency — confirm/add.
   - Template renderer that materialises `entrypoint.sh` with spec values at deploy time, so the baked docker image stays generic while the per-deploy entrypoint carries the config.
   - Claude auth path in the rendered entrypoint: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env is set, run non-interactive auth (investigate what `claude` CLI exposes for this — `claude setup-token` or similar; document whatever you find).
   - Railway provider plugin: thin wrapper over `railway` CLI (`up`, `down`, `ssh`, `variables --set`, `logs`, `status`). Live at `megaplan/cloud/providers/railway.py` with a `Provider` abstract base at `megaplan/cloud/providers/base.py` ready for sprint-2 plugins.

2. New argparse subcommands wired into `megaplan/cli.py`:
   - `megaplan cloud init` — scaffold `cloud.yaml` at project root
   - `megaplan cloud build` — docker build the image
   - `megaplan cloud deploy` — render entrypoint, upload vars, `railway up --detach --ci`
   - `megaplan cloud status` — invoke `megaplan status` remotely via provider ssh, return structured JSON (do NOT reinvent a parser — reuse what `megaplan status` already emits)
   - `megaplan cloud attach` — attach to tmux `agent` session
   - `megaplan cloud logs` — tail remote logs
   - `megaplan cloud exec "<cmd>"` — run arbitrary remote command (replaces README one-liners)
   - `megaplan cloud resume` — read remote plan state, dispatch `next_step`
   - `megaplan cloud down` — pause without deleting volume
   - `megaplan cloud destroy` — full teardown

3. Documentation at `docs/cloud.md`: env-var / cloud.yaml reference, symptom→cause→fix table (port from existing README), secret-rotation and cost-monitoring pointers.

4. Tests:
   - Unit: spec loader (happy path + validation errors)
   - Unit: template renderer (all hardcoded strings correctly replaced)
   - Unit: Railway provider with mocked subprocess
   - Smoke: `docker build` on the generated Dockerfile must succeed (CI-runnable; can be skipped on systems without docker with a clear warning)

5. Reigh parity validation (success criterion, not a test to automate): after implementation, the existing `reigh-megaplan-dev` behavior can be reproduced by `megaplan cloud deploy` with a `cloud.yaml` matching reigh's current env vars. The validation itself can be deferred to a follow-up runbook; the code must make it possible.

### Explicit non-goals for sprint 1
- Do NOT ship fly / ssh / local providers — that is sprint 2.
- Do NOT ship `cloud init-plan` bootstrap — sprint 2.
- Do NOT add a `toolchains:` block in `cloud.yaml` — sprint 2.
- Do NOT retire `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — it keeps running in parallel until sprint 2 migrates reigh fully.

### Constraints (hard requirements)
- Sprint 1 must be independently shippable: if sprint 2 slips, this release is still useful on its own.
- Preserve the idempotency contract of the current entrypoint (repo clone only if missing; codex config always overwritten on boot; megaplan always upgraded on boot).
- Preserve `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in the generated codex config with an explanatory comment — the container IS the sandbox.
- Preserve the `MEGAPLAN_REF` pinning mechanism, now surfaced as `megaplan.ref` in `cloud.yaml` (defaults to `main`).
- `railway` CLI is an acceptable runtime dependency; document it and fail gracefully with a link if missing.
- Do not break existing megaplan commands — `cloud` is additive.

### References
- Existing source at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — read everything.
- Target subpackage location: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/megaplan/cloud/`.
- Current CLI wiring pattern: `megaplan/cli.py` uses argparse with `subparsers.add_parser(...)` (see lines ~830-1005).
- Verified launcher for megaplan commands: `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan ...`. Bare `python` resolves to 3.8.10 which fails on `NotRequired`; the repo venv has 3.11.

The renderer emits only `megaplan config set agents.<step> <agent>` lines.\n\n4. **`cloud resume` must reuse `megaplan.auto._phase_command()`.** Don't re-implement the `next_step \u2192 argv` translation. The `execute` phase has the special case `execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved` \u2014 getting this wrong breaks the most important path.\n\n5. **Dockerfile COPY paths are relative to the staged build context**, which `materialize_deploy_dir()` produces with `wrappers/` as a subdir. Do NOT use `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/...` paths \u2014 those don't exist in the build context. This is the FLAG-007 regression guard; the docker smoke test in T13 is specifically there to catch it.\n\n6. **`repo.workspace` is a spec field, not a constant.** Every place reigh hardcoded `/workspace/reigh-app` (git `safe.directory`, `REPO_DIR=`, clone destination, tmux `-c <path>`, remote `cd` commands) must come from `spec.repo.workspace`. Default is `/workspace/app`. Validate it's absolute.\n\n7. **`mode=auto` requires `auto.plan_name`** in the spec because `megaplan auto` requires `--plan <name>` (auto.py:489). The entrypoint bootstraps the plan dir with `megaplan init` on first boot if it doesn't exist.\n\n8. **Claude CLI non-interactive auth:** research `claude setup-token` or equivalent in the vendored reigh Dockerfile/docs; if no non-interactive path exists, the rendered entrypoint emits a warning and continues (never `exit 1`). Do not block deploy on claude auth failure.\n\n9. **Do NOT amend existing megaplan commands.** `cloud` is strictly additive \u2014 no changes to `COMMAND_HANDLERS`, no touching existing handlers. The only edit outside `megaplan/cloud/` is the two-line wiring in `megaplan/cli.py` (parser registration + dispatch) plus `.gitignore` and `pyproject.toml` for the `_reference/` exclusion.\n\n10. **Keep modules under ~400 lines.** The subpackage has clear seams (spec / template / provider base / railway / cli); no single file should try to do two of these jobs.\n\n11. **Python version**: repo venv is 3.11. The new code can use `str | None` union syntax, `dataclass`, etc. Don't import from `typing.NotRequired` if avoidable \u2014 existing CLI already has that trap in the 3.8 bare-python path.",

Build `megaplan cloud` — a new subpackage at `megaplan/cloud/` that provides a built-in, provider-agnostic cloud runner wired into the existing megaplan CLI. This is sprint 1 of a two-sprint effort; the goal here is operational parity with the existing Railway setup at `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`, nothing more.

### What exists today (to be generalised)
The folder `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` contains a working but hardcoded Railway deployment. Read every file there during prep. Key pieces:
- `Dockerfile` — Ubuntu 22.04 + pyenv/Python 3.11 + nvm/Node 20 + codex CLI + claude CLI + megaplan from git
- `entrypoint.sh` — idempotent boot: codex auth (OPENAI_API_KEY), codex `config.toml` (model=gpt-5.4, reasoning=high, sandbox_mode=danger-full-access, approval_policy=never), megaplan install/upgrade from `MEGAPLAN_REF`, megaplan config (all phases→codex, auto_approve=true, robustness=standard), repo clone, installs `mp-run`/`mp-supervise`/`mp-heartbeat` wrapper scripts (currently embedded as heredocs), starts tmux sessions `agent` and `heartbeat`, starts healthserver
- `healthserver.py` — tiny HTTP server on :8080 for Railway healthcheck
- `railway.toml` — build/deploy config, healthcheck, restart policy
- `chain.sh` — thin shim around `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain.yaml`
- `chain.yaml.example` — chain spec format
- `README.md` — recipes for status/attach/resume/abort/restart/teardown that need to become subcommands

Hardcoded things to parameterise: `banodoco/reigh-app.git`, `/workspace/reigh-app`, `gpt-5.4` model, `high` reasoning, `[REDACTED]` email, all-phases→codex routing, `standard` robustness. Bug to fix: Claude Code CLI is installed in the image but the entrypoint never authenticates it — add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` auth path.

### Sprint 1 deliverables
1. New subpackage `megaplan/cloud/` parallel to `megaplan/loop/` and `megaplan/chain.py`, with:
   - Package resources: ported Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, healthserver.py. Extract the mp-run/mp-supervise/mp-heartbeat bash scripts (currently embedded as heredocs in entrypoint.sh) into their own files under `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/`.
   - Spec loader for `cloud.yaml` (schema covers at minimum: `provider`, `repo.url`/`branch`, `agents.default` + optional per-phase map, `codex.model` + `reasoning`, `mode` = auto|chain|idle, `auto.idea_file`, `auto.robustness`, `chain.spec`, `megaplan.ref`, `resources.volume`/`port`, `secrets` name list). PyYAML is not yet a dependency — confirm/add.
   - Template renderer that materialises `entrypoint.sh` with spec values at deploy time, so the baked docker image stays generic while the per-deploy entrypoint carries the config.
   - Claude auth path in the rendered entrypoint: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env is set, run non-interactive auth (investigate what `claude` CLI exposes for this — `claude setup-token` or similar; document whatever you find).
   - Railway provider plugin: thin wrapper over `railway` CLI (`up`, `down`, `ssh`, `variables --set`, `logs`, `status`). Live at `megaplan/cloud/providers/railway.py` with a `Provider` abstract base at `megaplan/cloud/providers/base.py` ready for sprint-2 plugins.

2. New argparse subcommands wired into `megaplan/cli.py`:
   - `megaplan cloud init` — scaffold `cloud.yaml` at project root
   - `megaplan cloud build` — docker build the image
   - `megaplan cloud deploy` — render entrypoint, upload vars, `railway up --detach --ci`
   - `megaplan cloud status` — invoke `megaplan status` remotely via provider ssh, return structured JSON (do NOT reinvent a parser — reuse what `megaplan status` already emits)
   - `megaplan cloud attach` — attach to tmux `agent` session
   - `megaplan cloud logs` — tail remote logs
   - `megaplan cloud exec "<cmd>"` — run arbitrary remote command (replaces README one-liners)
   - `megaplan cloud resume` — read remote plan state, dispatch `next_step`
   - `megaplan cloud down` — pause without deleting volume
   - `megaplan cloud destroy` — full teardown

3. Documentation at `docs/cloud.md`: env-var / cloud.yaml reference, symptom→cause→fix table (port from existing README), secret-rotation and cost-monitoring pointers.

4. Tests:
   - Unit: spec loader (happy path + validation errors)
   - Unit: template renderer (all hardcoded strings correctly replaced)
   - Unit: Railway provider with mocked subprocess
   - Smoke: `docker build` on the generated Dockerfile must succeed (CI-runnable; can be skipped on systems without docker with a clear warning)

5. Reigh parity validation (success criterion, not a test to automate): after implementation, the existing `reigh-megaplan-dev` behavior can be reproduced by `megaplan cloud deploy` with a `cloud.yaml` matching reigh's current env vars. The validation itself can be deferred to a follow-up runbook; the code must make it possible.

### Explicit non-goals for sprint 1
- Do NOT ship fly / ssh / local providers — that is sprint 2.
- Do NOT ship `cloud init-plan` bootstrap — sprint 2.
- Do NOT add a `toolchains:` block in `cloud.yaml` — sprint 2.
- Do NOT retire `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — it keeps running in parallel until sprint 2 migrates reigh fully.

### Constraints (hard requirements)
- Sprint 1 must be independently shippable: if sprint 2 slips, this release is still useful on its own.
- Preserve the idempotency contract of the current entrypoint (repo clone only if missing; codex config always overwritten on boot; megaplan always upgraded on boot).
- Preserve `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in the generated codex config with an explanatory comment — the container IS the sandbox.
- Preserve the `MEGAPLAN_REF` pinning mechanism, now surfaced as `megaplan.ref` in `cloud.yaml` (defaults to `main`).
- `railway` CLI is an acceptable runtime dependency; document it and fail gracefully with a link if missing.
- Do not break existing megaplan commands — `cloud` is additive.

### References
- Existing source at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — read everything.
- Target subpackage location: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/megaplan/cloud/`.
- Current CLI wiring pattern: `megaplan/cli.py` uses argparse with `subparsers.add_parser(...)` (see lines ~830-1005).
- Verified launcher for megaplan commands: `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan ...`. Bare `python` resolves to 3.8.10 which fails on `NotRequired`; the repo venv has 3.11.

User notes and answers:
- Answers to plan questions from orchestrator: (1) reigh-megaplan-dev access: assume executor has read access to ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ — if sandboxed, copy contents in as reference files. The orchestrator has verified the directory is readable. (2) Model 'gpt-5.4' is a literal string matching reigh's current config; treat as configurable with that default. (3) Claude non-interactive auth: executor should research 'claude setup-token' or equivalent; if no non-interactive path exists, degrade to a clear warning at boot (do NOT block deploy). (4) 'megaplan cloud status' should accept optional --plan and auto-discover the active plan remotely if omitted. (5) 'megaplan cloud destroy' requires interactive confirm unless --yes is passed.
- Gate escalation answer: pick option (a) — strict reigh parity. Sprint 1 must NOT add file-upload automation (that's sprint 2 scope). For mode=auto, when ${IDEA_FILE} is missing at boot the entrypoint must warn-and-drop-to-idle (NOT exit 1), matching reigh's 'deploy → upload via railway ssh → restart' workflow. docs/cloud.md must document this manual-upload step explicitly. No 11th cloud upload subcommand; users use 'megaplan cloud exec' to upload via railway ssh + stdin, and a doc recipe shows the exact one-liner. This is the strictest reading of 'operational parity with reigh, nothing more' from the original idea brief.

> DEVELOPER

Execute the approved plan in the repository.

        Project directory:
        /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan

        Idea:
Build `megaplan cloud` — a new subpackage at `megaplan/cloud/` that provides a built-in, provider-agnostic cloud runner wired into the existing megaplan CLI. This is sprint 1 of a two-sprint effort; the goal here is operational parity with the existing Railway setup at `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`, nothing more.

### What exists today (to be generalised)
The folder `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` contains a working but hardcoded Railway deployment. Read every file there during prep. Key pieces:
- `Dockerfile` — Ubuntu 22.04 + pyenv/Python 3.11 + nvm/Node 20 + codex CLI + claude CLI + megaplan from git
- `entrypoint.sh` — idempotent boot: codex auth (OPENAI_API_KEY), codex `config.toml` (model=gpt-5.4, reasoning=high, sandbox_mode=danger-full-access, approval_policy=never), megaplan install/upgrade from `MEGAPLAN_REF`, megaplan config (all phases→codex, auto_approve=true, robustness=standard), repo clone, installs `mp-run`/`mp-supervise`/`mp-heartbeat` wrapper scripts (currently embedded as heredocs), starts tmux sessions `agent` and `heartbeat`, starts healthserver
- `healthserver.py` — tiny HTTP server on :8080 for Railway healthcheck
- `railway.toml` — build/deploy config, healthcheck, restart policy
- `chain.sh` — thin shim around `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain.yaml`
- `chain.yaml.example` — chain spec format
- `README.md` — recipes for status/attach/resume/abort/restart/teardown that need to become subcommands

Hardcoded things to parameterise: `banodoco/reigh-app.git`, `/workspace/reigh-app`, `gpt-5.4` model, `high` reasoning, `[REDACTED]` email, all-phases→codex routing, `standard` robustness. Bug to fix: Claude Code CLI is installed in the image but the entrypoint never authenticates it — add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` auth path.

### Sprint 1 deliverables
1. New subpackage `megaplan/cloud/` parallel to `megaplan/loop/` and `megaplan/chain.py`, with:
   - Package resources: ported Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, healthserver.py. Extract the mp-run/mp-supervise/mp-heartbeat bash scripts (currently embedded as heredocs in entrypoint.sh) into their own files under `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/`.
   - Spec loader for `cloud.yaml` (schema covers at minimum: `provider`, `repo.url`/`branch`, `agents.default` + optional per-phase map, `codex.model` + `reasoning`, `mode` = auto|chain|idle, `auto.idea_file`, `auto.robustness`, `chain.spec`, `megaplan.ref`, `resources.volume`/`port`, `secrets` name list). PyYAML is not yet a dependency — confirm/add.
   - Template renderer that materialises `entrypoint.sh` with spec values at deploy time, so the baked docker image stays generic while the per-deploy entrypoint carries the config.
   - Claude auth path in the rendered entrypoint: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env is set, run non-interactive auth (investigate what `claude` CLI exposes for this — `claude setup-token` or similar; document whatever you find).
   - Railway provider plugin: thin wrapper over `railway` CLI (`up`, `down`, `ssh`, `variables --set`, `logs`, `status`). Live at `megaplan/cloud/providers/railway.py` with a `Provider` abstract base at `megaplan/cloud/providers/base.py` ready for sprint-2 plugins.

2. New argparse subcommands wired into `megaplan/cli.py`:
   - `megaplan cloud init` — scaffold `cloud.yaml` at project root
   - `megaplan cloud build` — docker build the image
   - `megaplan cloud deploy` — render entrypoint, upload vars, `railway up --detach --ci`
   - `megaplan cloud status` — invoke `megaplan status` remotely via provider ssh, return structured JSON (do NOT reinvent a parser — reuse what `megaplan status` already emits)
   - `megaplan cloud attach` — attach to tmux `agent` session
   - `megaplan cloud logs` — tail remote logs
   - `megaplan cloud exec "<cmd>"` — run arbitrary remote command (replaces README one-liners)
   - `megaplan cloud resume` — read remote plan state, dispatch `next_step`
   - `megaplan cloud down` — pause without deleting volume
   - `megaplan cloud destroy` — full teardown

3. Documentation at `docs/cloud.md`: env-var / cloud.yaml reference, symptom→cause→fix table (port from existing README), secret-rotation and cost-monitoring pointers.

4. Tests:
   - Unit: spec loader (happy path + validation errors)
   - Unit: template renderer (all hardcoded strings correctly replaced)
   - Unit: Railway provider with mocked subprocess
   - Smoke: `docker build` on the generated Dockerfile must succeed (CI-runnable; can be skipped on systems without docker with a clear warning)

5. Reigh parity validation (success criterion, not a test to automate): after implementation, the existing `reigh-megaplan-dev` behavior can be reproduced by `megaplan cloud deploy` with a `cloud.yaml` matching reigh's current env vars. The validation itself can be deferred to a follow-up runbook; the code must make it possible.

### Explicit non-goals for sprint 1
- Do NOT ship fly / ssh / local providers — that is sprint 2.
- Do NOT ship `cloud init-plan` bootstrap — sprint 2.
- Do NOT add a `toolchains:` block in `cloud.yaml` — sprint 2.
- Do NOT retire `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — it keeps running in parallel until sprint 2 migrates reigh fully.

### Constraints (hard requirements)
- Sprint 1 must be independently shippable: if sprint 2 slips, this release is still useful on its own.
- Preserve the idempotency contract of the current entrypoint (repo clone only if missing; codex config always overwritten on boot; megaplan always upgraded on boot).
- Preserve `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in the generated codex config with an explanatory comment — the container IS the sandbox.
- Preserve the `MEGAPLAN_REF` pinning mechanism, now surfaced as `megaplan.ref` in `cloud.yaml` (defaults to `main`).
- `railway` CLI is an acceptable runtime dependency; document it and fail gracefully with a link if missing.
- Do not break existing megaplan commands — `cloud` is additive.

### References
- Existing source at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — read everything.
- Target subpackage location: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/megaplan/cloud/`.
- Current CLI wiring pattern: `megaplan/cli.py` uses argparse with `subparsers.add_parser(...)` (see lines ~830-1005).
- Verified launcher for megaplan commands: `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan ...`. Bare `python` resolves to 3.8.10 which fails on `NotRequired`; the repo venv has 3.11.

This is the strictest reading of 'operational parity with reigh, nothing more' from the original idea brief.

    "Rendered entrypoint.sh must preserve idempotency: repo clone only if missing, codex config.toml always overwritten on boot, megaplan always reinstalled from MEGAPLAN_REF on boot, and `sandbox_mode = \"danger-full-access\"` kept with the 'container IS the sandbox' comment.",

    "Remote command name is `megaplan` (container installs it globally). Do NOT use `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan` for any remote/container command \u2014 only for local dev invocations against the repo venv.",
    "`megaplan config set` only accepts `agents.<step>` keys validated against `DEFAULT_AGENT_ROUTING`. The renderer must emit that exact shape \u2014 no `phase_agent.*` namespace.",
    "`cloud resume` must call `from megaplan.auto import _phase_command` and use the returned argv. The `execute` phase expands to `execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved`; re-implementing the translation risks missing that special case.",
    "`mode=auto` requires `auto.plan_name` in the spec because `megaplan auto` requires `--plan <name>` (auto.py:489). The entrypoint bootstraps the plan dir with `megaplan init` on first boot only if the plan dir doesn't already exist (preserving idempotency across restarts).",
    "Every place reigh hardcoded `/workspace/reigh-app` must use `${WORKSPACE_PATH}` sourced from `spec.repo.workspace` \u2014 git `safe.directory`, REPO_DIR, clone destination, tmux `-c`, and every remote `cd` command. Missing any site will cause parity drift.",

    "`railway` CLI is a runtime dependency \u2014 detect with `shutil.which` and raise `CliError('provider_unavailable', 'Install: https://docs.railway.app/develop/cli')` if missing. Do NOT assume it's installed.",
    "Missing-secret validation must happen BEFORE any `railway` subprocess calls in `deploy()` \u2014 otherwise users get a partial deploy.",
    "`cloud destroy` defaults to interactive confirm (prompt naming the volume); only `--yes` skips. `destroy(volume=...)` runs `railway down` first, THEN `railway volume delete <volume>` \u2014 non-zero exit on delete surfaces as `CliError('provider_failed', ...)`.",

        Idea:
Build `megaplan cloud` — a new subpackage at `megaplan/cloud/` that provides a built-in, provider-agnostic cloud runner wired into the existing megaplan CLI. This is sprint 1 of a two-sprint effort; the goal here is operational parity with the existing Railway setup at `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`, nothing more.

### What exists today (to be generalised)
The folder `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` contains a working but hardcoded Railway deployment. Read every file there during prep. Key pieces:
- `Dockerfile` — Ubuntu 22.04 + pyenv/Python 3.11 + nvm/Node 20 + codex CLI + claude CLI + megaplan from git
- `entrypoint.sh` — idempotent boot: codex auth (OPENAI_API_KEY), codex `config.toml` (model=gpt-5.4, reasoning=high, sandbox_mode=danger-full-access, approval_policy=never), megaplan install/upgrade from `MEGAPLAN_REF`, megaplan config (all phases→codex, auto_approve=true, robustness=standard), repo clone, installs `mp-run`/`mp-supervise`/`mp-heartbeat` wrapper scripts (currently embedded as heredocs), starts tmux sessions `agent` and `heartbeat`, starts healthserver
- `healthserver.py` — tiny HTTP server on :8080 for Railway healthcheck
- `railway.toml` — build/deploy config, healthcheck, restart policy
- `chain.sh` — thin shim around `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain.yaml`
- `chain.yaml.example` — chain spec format
- `README.md` — recipes for status/attach/resume/abort/restart/teardown that need to become subcommands

Hardcoded things to parameterise: `banodoco/reigh-app.git`, `/workspace/reigh-app`, `gpt-5.4` model, `high` reasoning, `[REDACTED]` email, all-phases→codex routing, `standard` robustness. Bug to fix: Claude Code CLI is installed in the image but the entrypoint never authenticates it — add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` auth path.

### Sprint 1 deliverables
1. New subpackage `megaplan/cloud/` parallel to `megaplan/loop/` and `megaplan/chain.py`, with:
   - Package resources: ported Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, healthserver.py. Extract the mp-run/mp-supervise/mp-heartbeat bash scripts (currently embedded as heredocs in entrypoint.sh) into their own files under `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/`.
   - Spec loader for `cloud.yaml` (schema covers at minimum: `provider`, `repo.url`/`branch`, `agents.default` + optional per-phase map, `codex.model` + `reasoning`, `mode` = auto|chain|idle, `auto.idea_file`, `auto.robustness`, `chain.spec`, `megaplan.ref`, `resources.volume`/`port`, `secrets` name list). PyYAML is not yet a dependency — confirm/add.
   - Template renderer that materialises `entrypoint.sh` with spec values at deploy time, so the baked docker image stays generic while the per-deploy entrypoint carries the config.
   - Claude auth path in the rendered entrypoint: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env is set, run non-interactive auth (investigate what `claude` CLI exposes for this — `claude setup-token` or similar; document whatever you find).
   - Railway provider plugin: thin wrapper over `railway` CLI (`up`, `down`, `ssh`, `variables --set`, `logs`, `status`). Live at `megaplan/cloud/providers/railway.py` with a `Provider` abstract base at `megaplan/cloud/providers/base.py` ready for sprint-2 plugins.

2. New argparse subcommands wired into `megaplan/cli.py`:
   - `megaplan cloud init` — scaffold `cloud.yaml` at project root
   - `megaplan cloud build` — docker build the image
   - `megaplan cloud deploy` — render entrypoint, upload vars, `railway up --detach --ci`
   - `megaplan cloud status` — invoke `megaplan status` remotely via provider ssh, return structured JSON (do NOT reinvent a parser — reuse what `megaplan status` already emits)
   - `megaplan cloud attach` — attach to tmux `agent` session
   - `megaplan cloud logs` — tail remote logs
   - `megaplan cloud exec "<cmd>"` — run arbitrary remote command (replaces README one-liners)
   - `megaplan cloud resume` — read remote plan state, dispatch `next_step`
   - `megaplan cloud down` — pause without deleting volume
   - `megaplan cloud destroy` — full teardown

3. Documentation at `docs/cloud.md`: env-var / cloud.yaml reference, symptom→cause→fix table (port from existing README), secret-rotation and cost-monitoring pointers.

4. Tests:
   - Unit: spec loader (happy path + validation errors)
   - Unit: template renderer (all hardcoded strings correctly replaced)
   - Unit: Railway provider with mocked subprocess
   - Smoke: `docker build` on the generated Dockerfile must succeed (CI-runnable; can be skipped on systems without docker with a clear warning)

Reigh parity validation (success criterion, not a test to automate): after implementation, the existing `reigh-megaplan-dev` behavior can be reproduced by `megaplan cloud deploy` with a `cloud.yaml` matching reigh's current env vars. The validation itself can be deferred to a follow-up runbook; the code must make it possible.

### Constraints (hard requirements)

- Preserve the `MEGAPLAN_REF` pinning mechanism, now surfaced as `megaplan.ref` in `cloud.yaml` (defaults to `main`).
- `railway` CLI is an acceptable runtime dependency; document it and fail gracefully with a link if missing.
- Do not break existing megaplan commands — `cloud` is additive.

Every subparser accepts `--cloud-yaml PATH` (default `<root>/cloud.yaml`). `status` and `resume` accept optional `--plan NAME`. `attach` accepts `--session NAME` override. `logs` accepts `--no-follow`. `exec` takes a single positional `command` string. `destroy` accepts `--yes` to skip interactive confirm. Implement `run_cloud_cli(root, args) -> int` modelled on `chain.py:528-555` dispatch pattern. Per-action behavior: `init` copies `templates/cloud.yaml.tmpl` to `<root>/cloud.yaml` (refuse overwrite without `--force`); `build` \u2192 `materialize_deploy_dir` then `provider.build(deploy_dir)`; `deploy` \u2192 render, gather secrets from `os.environ` for each name in `spec.secrets`, then `provider.deploy(deploy_dir, secrets=...)`; `status` \u2192 `provider.status_payload(plan=args.plan, workspace=spec.repo.workspace)` then print JSON; `attach` \u2192 `provider.attach()`; `logs` \u2192 `provider.logs(follow=not args.no_follow)`; `exec` \u2192 `provider.ssh_exec(args.command)` (NO auto-cd); `resume` \u2192 call `provider.status_payload(...)` to read `next_step`, then `from megaplan.auto import _phase_command; argv = _phase_command(next_step)`, construct remote command `cd <spec.repo.workspace> && megaplan <shell-quoted argv>` (append `--plan <args.plan>` if user supplied), then `provider.ssh_exec(...)`; `down` \u2192 `provider.down()`; `destroy` \u2192 if not `args.yes`, interactive prompt naming `spec.resources.volume`; then `provider.destroy(volume=spec.resources.volume)`. ### What exists today (to be generalised)
The folder `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` contains a working but hardcoded Railway deployment. Read every file there during prep. Key pieces:

- `entrypoint.sh` — idempotent boot: codex auth (OPENAI_API_KEY), codex `config.toml` (model=gpt-5.4, reasoning=high, sandbox_mode=danger-full-access, approval_policy=never), megaplan install/upgrade from `MEGAPLAN_REF`, megaplan config (all phases→codex, auto_approve=true, robustness=standard), repo clone, installs `mp-run`/`mp-supervise`/`mp-heartbeat` wrapper scripts (currently embedded as heredocs), starts tmux sessions `agent` and `heartbeat`, starts healthserver
- `healthserver.py` — tiny HTTP server on :8080 for Railway healthcheck

        Idea:
Build `megaplan cloud` — a new subpackage at `megaplan/cloud/` that provides a built-in, provider-agnostic cloud runner wired into the existing megaplan CLI. This is sprint 1 of a two-sprint effort; the goal here is operational parity with the existing Railway setup at `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`, nothing more.

### What exists today (to be generalised)
The folder `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` contains a working but hardcoded Railway deployment. Read every file there during prep. Key pieces:
- `Dockerfile` — Ubuntu 22.04 + pyenv/Python 3.11 + nvm/Node 20 + codex CLI + claude CLI + megaplan from git
- `entrypoint.sh` — idempotent boot: codex auth (OPENAI_API_KEY), codex `config.toml` (model=gpt-5.4, reasoning=high, sandbox_mode=danger-full-access, approval_policy=never), megaplan install/upgrade from `MEGAPLAN_REF`, megaplan config (all phases→codex, auto_approve=true, robustness=standard), repo clone, installs `mp-run`/`mp-supervise`/`mp-heartbeat` wrapper scripts (currently embedded as heredocs), starts tmux sessions `agent` and `heartbeat`, starts healthserver
- `healthserver.py` — tiny HTTP server on :8080 for Railway healthcheck
- `railway.toml` — build/deploy config, healthcheck, restart policy
- `chain.sh` — thin shim around `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain.yaml`
- `chain.yaml.example` — chain spec format
- `README.md` — recipes for status/attach/resume/abort/restart/teardown that need to become subcommands

Hardcoded things to parameterise: `banodoco/reigh-app.git`, `/workspace/reigh-app`, `gpt-5.4` model, `high` reasoning, `[REDACTED]` email, all-phases→codex routing, `standard` robustness. Bug to fix: Claude Code CLI is installed in the image but the entrypoint never authenticates it — add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` auth path.

### Sprint 1 deliverables
1. New subpackage `megaplan/cloud/` parallel to `megaplan/loop/` and `megaplan/chain.py`, with:
   - Package resources: ported Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, healthserver.py. Extract the mp-run/mp-supervise/mp-heartbeat bash scripts (currently embedded as heredocs in entrypoint.sh) into their own files under `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/`.
   - Spec loader for `cloud.yaml` (schema covers at minimum: `provider`, `repo.url`/`branch`, `agents.default` + optional per-phase map, `codex.model` + `reasoning`, `mode` = auto|chain|idle, `auto.idea_file`, `auto.robustness`, `chain.spec`, `megaplan.ref`, `resources.volume`/`port`, `secrets` name list). PyYAML is not yet a dependency — confirm/add.
   - Template renderer that materialises `entrypoint.sh` with spec values at deploy time, so the baked docker image stays generic while the per-deploy entrypoint carries the config.
   - Claude auth path in the rendered entrypoint: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env is set, run non-interactive auth (investigate what `claude` CLI exposes for this — `claude setup-token` or similar; document whatever you find).
   - Railway provider plugin: thin wrapper over `railway` CLI (`up`, `down`, `ssh`, `variables --set`, `logs`, `status`). Live at `megaplan/cloud/providers/railway.py` with a `Provider` abstract base at `megaplan/cloud/providers/base.py` ready for sprint-2 plugins.

2. New argparse subcommands wired into `megaplan/cli.py`:
   - `megaplan cloud init` — scaffold `cloud.yaml` at project root
   - `megaplan cloud build` — docker build the image
   - `megaplan cloud deploy` — render entrypoint, upload vars, `railway up --detach --ci`
   - `megaplan cloud status` — invoke `megaplan status` remotely via provider ssh, return structured JSON (do NOT reinvent a parser — reuse what `megaplan status` already emits)
   - `megaplan cloud attach` — attach to tmux `agent` session
   - `megaplan cloud logs` — tail remote logs
   - `megaplan cloud exec "<cmd>"` — run arbitrary remote command (replaces README one-liners)
   - `megaplan cloud resume` — read remote plan state, dispatch `next_step`
   - `megaplan cloud down` — pause without deleting volume
   - `megaplan cloud destroy` — full teardown

3. Documentation at `docs/cloud.md`: env-var / cloud.yaml reference, symptom→cause→fix table (port from existing README), secret-rotation and cost-monitoring pointers.

4. Tests:
   - Unit: spec loader (happy path + validation errors)
   - Unit: template renderer (all hardcoded strings correctly replaced)
   - Unit: Railway provider with mocked subprocess
   - Smoke: `docker build` on the generated Dockerfile must succeed (CI-runnable; can be skipped on systems without docker with a clear warning)

5. Reigh parity validation (success criterion, not a test to automate): after implementation, the existing `reigh-megaplan-dev` behavior can be reproduced by `megaplan cloud deploy` with a `cloud.yaml` matching reigh's current env vars. The validation itself can be deferred to a follow-up runbook; the code must make it possible.

### Explicit non-goals for sprint 1
- Do NOT ship fly / ssh / local providers — that is sprint 2.
- Do NOT ship `cloud init-plan` bootstrap — sprint 2.
- Do NOT add a `toolchains:` block in `cloud.yaml` — sprint 2.

- `railway` CLI is an acceptable runtime dependency; document it and fail gracefully with a link if missing.
- Do not break existing megaplan commands — `cloud` is additive.

        Idea:
Build `megaplan cloud` — a new subpackage at `megaplan/cloud/` that provides a built-in, provider-agnostic cloud runner wired into the existing megaplan CLI. This is sprint 1 of a two-sprint effort; the goal here is operational parity with the existing Railway setup at `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/`, nothing more.

### What exists today (to be generalised)
The folder `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` contains a working but hardcoded Railway deployment. Read every file there during prep. Key pieces:
- `Dockerfile` — Ubuntu 22.04 + pyenv/Python 3.11 + nvm/Node 20 + codex CLI + claude CLI + megaplan from git
- `entrypoint.sh` — idempotent boot: codex auth (OPENAI_API_KEY), codex `config.toml` (model=gpt-5.4, reasoning=high, sandbox_mode=danger-full-access, approval_policy=never), megaplan install/upgrade from `MEGAPLAN_REF`, megaplan config (all phases→codex, auto_approve=true, robustness=standard), repo clone, installs `mp-run`/`mp-supervise`/`mp-heartbeat` wrapper scripts (currently embedded as heredocs), starts tmux sessions `agent` and `heartbeat`, starts healthserver
- `healthserver.py` — tiny HTTP server on :8080 for Railway healthcheck
- `railway.toml` — build/deploy config, healthcheck, restart policy
- `chain.sh` — thin shim around `megaplan chain --spec /workspace/chain.yaml`
- `chain.yaml.example` — chain spec format
- `README.md` — recipes for status/attach/resume/abort/restart/teardown that need to become subcommands

Hardcoded things to parameterise: `banodoco/reigh-app.git`, `/workspace/reigh-app`, `gpt-5.4` model, `high` reasoning, `[REDACTED]` email, all-phases→codex routing, `standard` robustness. Bug to fix: Claude Code CLI is installed in the image but the entrypoint never authenticates it — add an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` auth path.

### Sprint 1 deliverables
1. New subpackage `megaplan/cloud/` parallel to `megaplan/loop/` and `megaplan/chain.py`, with:
   - Package resources: ported Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh, healthserver.py. Extract the mp-run/mp-supervise/mp-heartbeat bash scripts (currently embedded as heredocs in entrypoint.sh) into their own files under `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/`.
   - Spec loader for `cloud.yaml` (schema covers at minimum: `provider`, `repo.url`/`branch`, `agents.default` + optional per-phase map, `codex.model` + `reasoning`, `mode` = auto|chain|idle, `auto.idea_file`, `auto.robustness`, `chain.spec`, `megaplan.ref`, `resources.volume`/`port`, `secrets` name list). PyYAML is not yet a dependency — confirm/add.
   - Template renderer that materialises `entrypoint.sh` with spec values at deploy time, so the baked docker image stays generic while the per-deploy entrypoint carries the config.
   - Claude auth path in the rendered entrypoint: if `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env is set, run non-interactive auth (investigate what `claude` CLI exposes for this — `claude setup-token` or similar; document whatever you find).
   - Railway provider plugin: thin wrapper over `railway` CLI (`up`, `down`, `ssh`, `variables --set`, `logs`, `status`). Live at `megaplan/cloud/providers/railway.py` with a `Provider` abstract base at `megaplan/cloud/providers/base.py` ready for sprint-2 plugins.

2. New argparse subcommands wired into `megaplan/cli.py`:
   - `megaplan cloud init` — scaffold `cloud.yaml` at project root
   - `megaplan cloud build` — docker build the image
   - `megaplan cloud deploy` — render entrypoint, upload vars, `railway up --detach --ci`
   - `megaplan cloud status` — invoke `megaplan status` remotely via provider ssh, return structured JSON (do NOT reinvent a parser — reuse what `megaplan status` already emits)
   - `megaplan cloud attach` — attach to tmux `agent` session
   - `megaplan cloud logs` — tail remote logs
   - `megaplan cloud exec "<cmd>"` — run arbitrary remote command (replaces README one-liners)
   - `megaplan cloud resume` — read remote plan state, dispatch `next_step`
   - `megaplan cloud down` — pause without deleting volume
   - `megaplan cloud destroy` — full teardown

3. Documentation at `docs/cloud.md`: env-var / cloud.yaml reference, symptom→cause→fix table (port from existing README), secret-rotation and cost-monitoring pointers.

4. Tests:
   - Unit: spec loader (happy path + validation errors)
   - Unit: template renderer (all hardcoded strings correctly replaced)
   - Unit: Railway provider with mocked subprocess
   - Smoke: `docker build` on the generated Dockerfile must succeed (CI-runnable; can be skipped on systems without docker with a clear warning)

5. Reigh parity validation (success criterion, not a test to automate): after implementation, the existing `reigh-megaplan-dev` behavior can be reproduced by `megaplan cloud deploy` with a `cloud.yaml` matching reigh's current env vars. The validation itself can be deferred to a follow-up runbook; the code must make it possible.

### Explicit non-goals for sprint 1
- Do NOT ship fly / ssh / local providers — that is sprint 2.
- Do NOT ship `cloud init-plan` bootstrap — sprint 2.
- Do NOT add a `toolchains:` block in `cloud.yaml` — sprint 2.
- Do NOT retire `~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — it keeps running in parallel until sprint 2 migrates reigh fully.

### Constraints (hard requirements)
- Sprint 1 must be independently shippable: if sprint 2 slips, this release is still useful on its own.
- Preserve the idempotency contract of the current entrypoint (repo clone only if missing; codex config always overwritten on boot; megaplan always upgraded on boot).
- Preserve `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` in the generated codex config with an explanatory comment — the container IS the sandbox.
- Preserve the `MEGAPLAN_REF` pinning mechanism, now surfaced as `megaplan.ref` in `cloud.yaml` (defaults to `main`).
- `railway` CLI is an acceptable runtime dependency; document it and fail gracefully with a link if missing.
- Do not break existing megaplan commands — `cloud` is additive.

### References
- Existing source at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/` — read everything.
- Target subpackage location: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/megaplan/megaplan/cloud/`.
- Current CLI wiring pattern: `megaplan/cli.py` uses argparse with `subparsers.add_parser(...)` (see lines ~830-1005).
- Verified launcher for megaplan commands: `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan ...`. Bare `python` resolves to 3.8.10 which fails on `NotRequired`; the repo venv has 3.11.

User notes and answers:
- Answers to plan questions from orchestrator: (1) reigh-megaplan-dev access: assume executor has read access to ~/Documents/reigh-megaplan-dev/ — if sandboxed, copy contents in as reference files. The orchestrator has verified the directory is readable. (2) Model 'gpt-5.4' is a literal string matching reigh's current config; treat as configurable with that default. (3) Claude non-interactive auth: executor should research 'claude setup-token' or equivalent; if no non-interactive path exists, degrade to a clear warning at boot (do NOT block deploy). (4) 'megaplan cloud status' should accept optional --plan and auto-discover the active plan remotely if omitted. (5) 'megaplan cloud destroy' requires interactive confirm unless --yes is passed.
- Gate escalation answer: pick option (a) — strict reigh parity. Sprint 1 must NOT add file-upload automation (that's sprint 2 scope). For mode=auto, when ${IDEA_FILE} is missing at boot the entrypoint must warn-and-drop-to-idle (NOT exit 1), matching reigh's 'deploy → upload via railway ssh → restart' workflow. docs/cloud.md must document this manual-upload step explicitly. No 11th cloud upload subcommand; users use 'megaplan cloud exec' to upload via railway ssh + stdin, and a doc recipe shows the exact one-liner. This is the strictest reading of 'operational parity with reigh, nothing more' from the original idea brief.

The `execute` phase has the special case `execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved` \u2014 getting this wrong breaks the most important path.\n\n5. **Dockerfile COPY paths are relative to the staged build context**, which `materialize_deploy_dir()` produces with `wrappers/` as a subdir. Do NOT use `megaplan/cloud/wrappers/...` paths \u2014 those don't exist in the build context. This is the FLAG-007 regression guard; the docker smoke test in T13 is specifically there to catch it.\n\n6. **`repo.workspace` is a spec field, not a constant.** Every place reigh hardcoded `/workspace/reigh-app` (git `safe.directory`, `REPO_DIR=`, clone destination, tmux `-c <path>`, remote `cd` commands) must come from `spec.repo.workspace`. Default is `/workspace/app`. Validate it's absolute.\n\n7. **`mode=auto` requires `auto.plan_name`** in the spec because `megaplan auto` requires `--plan <name>` (auto.py:489). The entrypoint bootstraps the plan dir with `megaplan init` on first boot if it doesn't exist.\n\n8. **Claude CLI non-interactive auth:** research `claude setup-token` or equivalent in the vendored reigh Dockerfile/docs; if no non-interactive path exists, the rendered entrypoint emits a warning and continues (never `exit 1`). Do not block deploy on claude auth failure.\n\n9. **Do NOT amend existing megaplan commands.** `cloud` is strictly additive \u2014 no changes to `COMMAND_HANDLERS`, no touching existing handlers. The only edit outside `megaplan/cloud/` is the two-line wiring in `megaplan/cli.py` (parser registration + dispatch) plus `.gitignore` and `pyproject.toml` for the `_reference/` exclusion.\n\n10. **Keep modules under ~400 lines.** The subpackage has clear seams (spec / template / provider base / railway / cli); no single file should try to do two of these jobs.\n\n11. **Python version**: repo venv is 3.11.     "Remote command name is `megaplan` (container installs it globally). Do NOT use `./.venv/bin/python -m megaplan` for any remote/container command \u2014 only for local dev invocations against the repo venv.",
    "`megaplan config set` only accepts `agents.<step>` keys validated against `DEFAULT_AGENT_ROUTING`. The renderer must emit that exact shape \u2014 no `phase_agent.*` namespace.",
    "`cloud resume` must call `from megaplan.auto import _phase_command` and use the returned argv. The `execute` phase expands to `execute --confirm-destructive --user-approved`; re-implementing the translation risks missing that special case.",
    "`mode=auto` requires `auto.plan_name` in the spec because `megaplan auto` requires `--plan <name>` (auto.py:489). The entrypoint bootstraps the plan dir with `megaplan init` on first boot only if the plan dir doesn't already exist (preserving idempotency across restarts).",
    "Every place reigh hardcoded `/workspace/reigh-app` must use `${WORKSPACE_PATH}` sourced from `spec.repo.workspace` \u2014 git `safe.directory`, REPO_DIR, clone destination, tmux `-c`, and every remote `cd` command. Missing any site will cause parity drift.",

    "`railway` CLI is a runtime dependency \u2014 detect with `shutil.which` and raise `CliError('provider_unavailable', 'Install: https://docs.railway.app/develop/cli')` if missing. Do NOT assume it's installed.",
    "Missing-secret validation must happen BEFORE any `railway` subprocess calls in `deploy()` \u2014 otherwise users get a partial deploy.",
    "`cloud destroy` defaults to interactive confirm (prompt naming the volume); only `--yes` skips. `destroy(volume=...)` runs `railway down` first, THEN `railway volume delete <volume>` \u2014 non-zero exit on delete surfaces as `CliError('provider_failed', ...)`.",

 f\"Version: {version}\",\n        \"\",\n    ])\n\n\ndef _wheel() -> str:\n    return \"\\n\".join([\n        \"Wheel-Version: 1.0\",\n        \"Generator: temp-offline-backend\",\n f\"sha256={b64}\", str(len(data))\n\n\ndef build_wheel(wheel_directory, config_settings=None, metadata_directory=None):\n    root = Path.cwd()\n    name, version = _project_meta(root / record_text.append(','.join(row))\n        record_text.append(f\"{record_rel},,\")\n        record_bytes = ('\\n'.join(record_text) + '\\n').encode('utf-8')\n        zf.writestr(record_rel,
